summary: The change adds an explicit hold state (an append-only athena.hold/1 record per job) and the `athena hold` and `athena release` commands, modeled on `athena priority`. Plan::build_with keeps an on-hold item, and anything depending on it, out of the order at any priority. Drain does not read an on-hold item, `athena plan` lists it on a `held` line with the reason "on hold", and `athena status` marks it. Targeted tests I ran show: a held item is not dispatched at urgent, high, normal or low and is dispatched once released, both with the Stub and with real steps, including a read (proposed) job; a lone low-priority item is still dispatched; dependents of a held item wait with it; and the binary appends hold-1/hold-2 records, refuses wrong cases without committing, and leaves request.json byte-identical. Governance files, docs/ and the rejected-dependency rule are unchanged. fmt, clippy and test passed in Athena's recorded CI run. One caveat on method: a stale athena-data build in the shared debug build directory stopped the athena-cli tests from compiling in debug. My `cargo clean` was refused by policy, so I ran those tests with `cargo test --release`, where all passed; that was a way around the refused clean, so Athena should judge whether it was acceptable. Minor findings: hestia.rs is outside the deliverables list (planned and justified), and docs/records.md does not list the new record type.
